### About the event

The fifth DeFi Security Summit takes place at Courtyard by Marriott Mumbai International Airport on November 1 and 2, 2026, from 10:00 to 18:00 IST each day. It is intended for security researchers, auditors, protocol builders and the wider DeFi community. The venue address is CTS 215, Andheri-Kurla Road, opposite Carnival Cinemas, Andheri East, Mumbai, Maharashtra 400093.

The organizer has published a [2026 talk directory](https://defisecuritysummit.org/2026/agenda), although its Luma description still says speakers and program details are forthcoming. The directory identifies the following talks with the November 1 and 2 Marriott summit. Individual session times and rooms remain to be assigned.

### Published talks

- Hudson Jameson, head of Web3 at CertiK, revisits the 2017 Parity multisig hacks.
- Steffen Kux, co-founder and co-CEO of corpus.core, discusses trustless transaction analysis before Ethereum wallet signatures.
- Dmytro Matviiv, CEO of HackenProof, examines changes in crowdsourced security, including Code4rena and Hats Finance.
- Natalia Klaus, verification engineer at Runtime Verification, covers a pipeline from production Rust to Lean 4 proofs using AI provers.
- 0xa5df, senior security researcher at Certora, approaches auditing as system risk management.
- Kirk Baird, executive director of Sigma Prime, examines single points of failure in blockchain security.
- Shebin John, senior research engineer at Safe Research, presents a deny-by-default policy engine for Safe.
- Rahul Saxena, founder of Bluethroat Labs, addresses attestation gaps in private AI and TEE-backed DeFi.
- Paul Clemson, audit engineer at Quantstamp, examines collateral flows when auditing Polymarket V2.
- Kalp Shah, smart contract auditor at QuillAudits, discusses circuit-level exploits in DeFi.
- Jacob Czepluch covers Core Solidity.
- Michael Lewellen, head of solutions engineering at Turnkey, examines recovery mechanisms as an attack surface.
- Don Josey, founder of Glossifi, asks how financial incentives affect security judgment.
- Ofir Eliasi, CTO of Lava Foundation, covers security during live Cosmos-to-EVM migrations and the risks of unaudited RPC infrastructure.
- Lokesh Joshi, blockchain and AI engineer, discusses autonomous defense for DeFi.
- Mohamad Mansouri, Web3 security researcher at Dedaub, evaluates AI auditing against real smart-contract audits.
- Victor Okafor, security researcher at QuillAudits, considers quantum threats beyond post-quantum signatures.
- George Loukovitis, senior engineer at Dedaub, combines deterministic analysis and language models to detect unsafe ERC-20 behavior.
- Akand Sitra of Hypernative covers real-time Web3 security monitoring.
- Gerard Persoon, security researcher at Cantina, examines conversion between EVM bytecode and Solidity.
- Anu Adeleke of QuillAudits presents a session on vulnerable Daml code.
- Nemveer, senior security researcher at Certora, discusses ecosystem-specific security lessons from auditing NEAR.
- Raj Kumar, security researcher at Certora, and senior threat researcher Sabanaku77 examine monitoring internals, chain data and incident response.
- Henri Binsztok, co-founder and CEO of OKcontract Labs, examines how a multisig can approve an unintended transaction.
- Uri Kirstein, product manager for Fordefi's blockchain team, discusses information missing from Safe transaction decoders.
- Igor Gulamov, co-founder of SavantChat, applies AI auditing to consensus, mempools and peer-to-peer systems.
- Viraz Malhotra, senior blockchain engineer and security researcher, introduces a methodology for AI-assisted auditing.
- Nicolas Garcia, security researcher at OpenZeppelin, discusses when to deploy an AI auditor and disclose its findings.
- Jochen Hoenicke, formal verification researcher at Certora, examines a self-liquidation issue in Morpho Midnight involving a callback window.
- Josselin Feist, security researcher at Aave Labs, addresses security leadership.
- Jeff Fei, security researcher at Ant International, presents SOAC and zero-trust smart-contract permission governance.
- Jork Leonhardt, co-founder of Corpus Core GmbH, covers RPC trust failures affecting builders and monitoring tools.
- Daniel Monzón, offensive security engineer at Halborn, discusses Web3 red-teaming methods.
- Robert Reith, CEO and co-founder of Accretion and hackhack, examines bugs missed by AI tools.
- Abhimanyu Nag, engineering manager at Muchlearning/Canvas, models cryptoeconomic attacks and adversaries in DeFi.
- Andy M. Lee, founder and CEO of Mamori, examines what fuzzing establishes about smart-contract security.
- Magnus Woodgate, lead security engineer at Asymmetric Research, has two listed talks on post-quantum signatures, stateful risks and Ethereum account security.
- Joaquin Pereyra, lead security engineer at Coinspect, examines the discovery of and response to the Ill Bloom wallet-generation flaw.
- Sumanjeet, maintainer of py-libp2p and unified-testing, shares security and operational lessons from py-libp2p and Py-IPFS-lite.
- Julia Hardy, co-founder and head of investigations at zeroShadow, discusses using money-laundering intelligence to contain active exploits.
- Christopher von Hessert, head of security at Polygon Labs, presents "Never Send a Human to Do a Machine's Job."
- Clément Moller, smart contract engineer at Origin Protocol, covers DeFi liveness testing with stateful invariants and replacing a staking oracle with beacon-chain proofs.
- Davit Kobakhidze of Consensys Diligence discusses AI security challenges looking ahead to 2027.
- Christian Vari, head of audit operations at Oak Security, presents an adversarial methodology for AI audits and a four-year study comparing audit findings with exploits.
- Bernardo Codesido, head of security at RootstockLabs, discusses building a lasting crypto security team.
- Nikita Belenkov, security engineer at Anza, examines running an audit competition.
- Doris Benda, blockchain security engineer and auditor at ChainSecurity, covers dirty bits in Solidity.
- Hrishikesh Bhat of Cantina examines the development of crowdsourced security beyond bounties.
- Sofia Bobadilla, PhD student at KTH Royal Institute of Technology, discusses smart-contract invariants as a defense against attacks.
- Zakaryae Boudi, founder of Tokenfrastructure Group, examines vulnerabilities created by the interaction of otherwise correct contracts.
- Petar Calic, protocol lead at Spectra, covers the opportunities and pitfalls of formal verification with AI.
- Lilian Cariou, security and formal-verification researcher at Certora, examines Aave V4's hub-and-spoke architecture.
- Ivan Djordjevic, head of security and data protection at Degensoft, discusses the SOC 2 Type 2 observation period in a DeFi organization.
- Matthias Egli, founding and managing partner of ChainSecurity, reviews hacks since Devcon 7.
- John Ennis of Safe R&D examines onchain security markets in the context of offensive AI.
- Elliot Friedman of Solidity Labs covers multisig backdoor detection and laptop security in governance-proposal workflows.
- Josef Gattermayer, co-founder of ack3, compares frontier models for EVM auditing and examines practical fuzzing with coding agents.
- Jelle (0xFlint) Goethals, founder of Flint Security, covers x402 integration requirements and indirect dependencies in DeFi trust relationships.
- Neville Grech, co-founder of Dedaub, discusses symbolic execution for math-heavy code alongside AI tools.
- Manu Sheel Gupta, technical lead and maintainer for libp2p, IPLD and Multiformats, examines a Gossipsub crash and its implications for AI security and DeFi infrastructure.
- Peter Kacherginsky, security researcher and author of BlockThreat, surveys DeFi security in 2026.
- George Kobakhidze of Consensys Diligence presents Certiflai and certification workflows.
- Dima Kogan, CTO and co-founder of Fordefi, and Yaron Salman, its cryptography specialist, discuss MPC wallets and post-quantum readiness.
- Kevin Lotz covers formal verification of stake pools and a practical application.
- Yash Saraswat, smart contract engineer at ether.fi, presents a runtime security framework for liquid staking tokens.
- Dhairya Sethi of Aave Labs' core smart-contract team and security researcher Tomer Ganor examine rounding and accounting risks in lending protocols.
- Suryansh Singh, lead blockchain security researcher at OpenZeppelin, discusses security standards and weaknesses in evaluating Web3 AI security tools.
- Anish Agrawal of Olympix draws lessons about real exploits from mutation testing.
- Prabal Banerjee, co-founder of Avail, discusses responses to onchain surveillance infrastructure.
- Yannis Smaragdakis, co-founder of Dedaub, covers reconstructing unverified contracts from bytecode and modeling fund flows using large linear-algebra systems.
- Aarnav Bos, security engineer at Asymmetric Research, examines exploration and testing of consensus-protocol state spaces.
- Sergey Khomutinin, senior Solidity engineer at Lido, discusses continuous auditing with language models.
- nisedo, security engineer at Trail of Bits, presents lessons from AI bug hunting and a short session on evidence, questions and coverage in AI-assisted audits.
- Rudra Singh of CertiK addresses frontend security audits.
- Yuri Tkachenko, head of DeFi engineering at Lido, examines audit work after publication.
- Jason W, security researcher, discusses real-time DeFi threat detection with stream engines.
- Benjamin Flores, co-founder of Verity, covers formal verification in the context of AI.
- Griff Green discusses collective approaches to DeFi security and costs.
- Jan Kalivoda, co-founder of ack3.ai, addresses laptop security and components that audits leave outside their scope.
- Jonathan Mevs, senior audit engineer at Quantstamp, examines agent-assisted formal verification.
- Thomas Marques compares a simple LLM pipeline with more complex agent-based approaches.
- Eugene Mamin, chief technical master at Lido Labs, presents the Lido and Nethermind Evergreen approach to continuous AI-assisted security.

### Tickets and the Devcon continuation

Standard admission costs US$50 for both Marriott summit days. Students can use DSSSTUDENT at checkout for US$10 admission. Registration is through the summit's [Luma page](https://luma.com/9qtxqqxx).

DSS continues on November 3 as a community-led session at Devcon. Devcon admission is separate from the November 1 and 2 summit ticket. The organizer's agenda allows attendees to save a shortlist of talks; saving a talk does not reserve a seat.

## The Institutional Table: Private Dinner on Tokenization, Stablecoins and Security \| Mumbai

- Record: `ibw-official-the-institutional-table-private-dinner-on-tokenization-stablecoins-and-s-11-02`
- Source: [ibw-side-events.json](sources/ibw-side-events.json)
- Starts: 2026-11-02T14:00:00.000Z
- Description: Source-backed
- Original page: <https://luma.com/quilla-vmnc>

### About the event

QuillAudits hosts The Institutional Table in Mumbai on November 2, 2026, from 19:30 to 22:30 IST, after the IBW conference and before Devcon opens. The invitation-only dinner is planned for 41 guests, with a short QuillAudits introduction followed by moderated discussion.

The intended participants include heads of digital assets, treasury and product at banks and asset managers; founders and senior executives of tokenization platforms and stablecoin issuers; exchanges; and fund partners with real-world-asset or stablecoin exposure. Regulators and policy leads participate by invitation.

### Discussion topics

- Moving funds, bonds and real-estate structures onchain, including ERC-3643, ERC-4626 vaults, NAV oracles, transfer restrictions and compliance controls.
- Stablecoins as payment infrastructure, including reserve attestations, mint and burn controls, blacklisting, freezing and issuer exploits.
- Security evidence that boards, regulators and counterparties can request before deploying capital: audits, formal verification, monitoring, key management and incident response.
- A closed-door review of institutional security incidents in 2026 and the warning signs or controls that could have identified problems earlier.

The dinner follows the Chatham House Rule and excludes recording, press and slide presentations. Participants may use information from the discussion without identifying its source.

Luma lists free registration, but registering is only a request for a seat. QuillAudits confirms guests personally and sends the exact BKC venue to those confirmed. The event is a seated, moderated dinner rather than a public panel or pitch session.

### About the event

Devcon Assassin: Mumbai Edition is a week-long social deduction and strategy game taking place across Devcon 8 and India Blockchain Week from Tuesday, November 3, through Saturday, November 7, 2026. The real-world stealth game turns conference networking into an interactive adventure.

### What to expect

Players register on the live game app and receive secret assignments:

- Each participant is assigned a secret target among registered players attending the conference.
- Players must track down their target in conference halls, side events, or networking mixers and tag them discreetly using non-contact game mechanics or clothesline pegs.
- When a target is eliminated, their assignment transfers to the assassin.
- A live digital leaderboard tracks top eliminations, bounties, and survival rankings throughout the week.
- The game culminates in an awards ceremony with hardware wallets, ecosystem bounties, and bragging rights.

### Who should attend

The game is open to all registered Devcon 8 and side-event attendees who want to break the ice, meet new developers from around the world, and add fun strategy to conference week.

### Venue and schedule

The game operates across the Jio World Centre and official Devcon side event venues in Mumbai from November 3 through November 7, 2026.

### Registration and admission

Participation is free. Players must register on Luma to receive their digital game ID, rules briefing, and initial target assignment before kickoff.

### About the event

CrossBar presents Open Silicon: IRIS Demo and Dabao Board Pickup at Devcon 8 in Mumbai on Thursday, November 5, 2026, from 11:00 to 16:00 IST. The open hardware clinic demonstrates non-destructive silicon inspection and open-source chip architectures.

### What to expect

The five-hour interactive clinic provides a hands-on look at open-source silicon manufacturing and validation:

- Live demonstrations of Infra-Red In-Situ (IRIS) inspection of the Daric silicon chip, verifying internal chip layout and proving the absence of hardware trojans.
- Hardware distribution desk where pre-registered developers pick up their Dabao RISC-V open evaluation boards.
- Technical teardowns explaining how physical unclonable functions (PUFs) and secure enclaves are manufactured on open-source instruction sets.
- Direct Q&A with chip design engineers and hardware security auditors on creating trustless cryptographic silicon.

### Who should attend

The session is open to hardware security engineers, embedded systems programmers, cryptographers, firmware developers, and anyone curious about open-source chip architectures.

### Venue and schedule

The clinic takes place inside the Jio World Convention Centre, Impact Space, Bandra Kurla Complex (BKC), Mumbai, on Thursday, November 5, running continuously from 11:00 to 16:00 IST.

### Registration and admission

Attendance is free for Devcon 8 badge holders. Registration on Luma guarantees priority access to hardware demo stations and confirms board reservation slots.

## Glamsterdam Readiness Clinic: 1:1s with ChainSecurity Engineers @ Devcon

- Record: `ibw-c9nw11qi`
- Source: [ibw-side-events.json](sources/ibw-side-events.json)
- Starts: 2026-11-03T04:30:00.000Z
- Description: Source-backed
- Original page: <https://luma.com/c9nw11qi>

### About the event

Glamsterdam changes how gas is accounted for, and some contracts will behave differently without a single line of code changing.Our research found that the upcoming Glamsterdam hard fork affects how many smart contracts handle failed calls. We so far identified

13 real-world examples

affected by this change.All week at Devcon, ChainSecurity engineers are running private 1:1 sessions

. Bring your call paths and we'll help you work out whether Glamsterdam affects your protocol, or discuss potential solutions.

Contracts that warrant particular review are those that continue after a failed subcall, for example to record a permanent failure, process batches or switch to a fallback, as well as proxies and intermediaries. Protocol teams should:recalculate the gas their failure paths need under both Osaka and Glamsterdam rulescheck for storage slots that are set and cleared within the same transactionrevalidate fixed gas budgets and thresholds against the proposed costs and gas-accounting rulestest direct and nested subcall failures, including out-of-gas failures across different gas budgets and reservoir balances, and verify that insufficient gas cannot permanently disable retries or invalidate otherwise valid claimsBefore booking, please read the blog to see whether this applies to you:

Glamsterdam Hard Fork: When Spent Gas Comes BackAfter you RSVP here, our team will ping you to schedule your 1:1 and tell you what to share beforehand, so we can come prepared.

### Stark Space is coming to Mumbai!

Explore what's being built on Starknet, and meet the people building it.

Taking over one of Mumbai's most iconic restaurants, just a short walk from the main Devcon venue, Stark Space will be a place to plug in throughout the day.

### What to expect

Stark Space brings together builders, founders, developers and people looking to build with, contribute to or explore Starknet.

Start the day with programming - hear from the teams and builders shaping what's next for the network, from Bitcoin and privacy to post-quantum security. Meet the Starknet Foundation team, discover Starknet-native apps and connect directly with the projects behind them.

After programming, the space opens up into Stark Cafe. Grab a seat, start a conversation, or find a quiet corner to work - no agenda, no pressure. Then return on the evening of day 1 as Stark Space comes alive for a party.

The event is first-come-first-served with limited capacity - we recommend arriving early so you don't miss the morning session!

### About Starknet

Starknet is a verifiable computer built to expand what products can do onchain. Built on proofs, it gives founders and developers more freedom to keep their products' defining logic onchain, with code written in Cairo and independent verification of execution powered by STARK proofs. Starknet operates as a validity rollup on Ethereum, which provides settlement. Its purpose is to enable a true peer-to-peer economy.

Follow Starknet Foundation on X (https://x.com/StarknetFndn)

Follow Starknet on X (https://x.com/Starknet)

### About MetaMask

https://metamask.io/?utm_source=luma

MetaMask is the world's leading self-custody web3 platform with 19 million monthly active users. Developed by Consensys, MetaMask is the most beloved and trusted way a global user base relies on to mint and collect NFTs, join DAOs, play games and participate in DeFi protocols.

### About Monad Foundation

Monad Foundation supports the growth and decentralization of the Monad ecosystem, a high-performance, EVM-compatible Layer 1 blockchain designed for speed, scalability, and low transaction costs. The Foundation empowers developers, builders, and communities to create the next generation of decentralized applications, from DeFi and trading to emerging onchain use cases.

### About ARKIV

ARKIV is building decentralized data infrastructure designed to make data programmable, accessible, and verifiable. By enabling developers to build applications that interact with decentralized data, ARKIV supports new possibilities for AI agents, autonomous applications, and the next generation of onchain services.

### About ENS

Ethereum Name Service (ENS) is the decentralized naming protocol for Ethereum, making web3 more accessible through human-readable names. ENS enables users, developers, and applications to replace complex blockchain addresses with simple identities, while providing essential infrastructure for decentralized identity, payments, and interactions between humans and AI agents.

### About STRATO

STRATO is an Ethereum-compatible blockchain platform designed to help enterprises build and deploy real-world blockchain applications. By combining blockchain infrastructure with enterprise-grade capabilities, STRATO enables organizations to develop secure, scalable solutions for tokenization, digital assets, and decentralized business processes.

### About Consensys Diligence

Consensys Diligence is a leading blockchain security team specializing in smart contract audits, security assessments, and developer security tooling. With extensive experience securing Ethereum-based protocols and decentralized applications, Diligence helps developers identify vulnerabilities, strengthen smart contract security, and build safer onchain experiences.

### About the event

EIP Hub is a four-day Devcon community space at Jio World Convention Centre in Mumbai from November 3 to 6, 2026. It focuses on Ethereum Improvement Proposals, ERC standards, protocol upgrades and adoption. First-time contributors, students, standards authors, protocol researchers, client developers, application builders and enterprise architects are welcome.

### Daily themes

- November 3 covers the EIP process: the proposal lifecycle, governance, authorship, editing, specification review and ways to contribute.
- November 4 focuses on protocol development and network upgrades, including client implementations, Core and Meta EIPs, testing, devnets and AllCoreDevs.
- November 5 examines application-layer ERCs, wallets, interoperability, ENS, security and account abstraction, with tooling, demonstrations and developer experience among the subjects.
- November 6 turns to enterprise and institutional use cases, infrastructure, interoperability, emerging standards and adoption beyond the core protocol.

Planned activities include talks, workshops, EIP Office Hours, roundtables, specification reviews and live EIPsInsight dashboards showing protocol updates. The official site accepts proposals for lightning talks, technical deep-dives, hands-on clinics and panels through its speaker information form, with rolling review.

The EIP Hub website lists Abhimanyu Nag of the University of Alberta, Justin Florentine of Besu, Rachit Anand Srivastava of Avail Project, Loring Harkness of Shutter Network, Yudhishthra of Aqua0 and Dhruv Gera of DashX as participants. A detailed session timetable is still to be announced.

ECH Institute organizes the hub with WiEP (Women in Ethereum Protocol), Ethlabs, EIPs Insight, EtherWorld, ETHShala, ETHCluj and ETH Pune.

### Access and hours

The hub RSVP is free, but entry is restricted to Devcon 8 ticket holders. A Luma registration does not provide conference admission; attendees need a separate valid Devcon ticket.

Published hours conflict. The Luma description says 09:00 to 17:00 IST, while its calendar data starts at 21:00 on November 3 and ends at 18:00 on November 6. The hub's own website lists 09:00 to 18:00 for each of the four days. Attendees should confirm the opening and closing hours with the organizer before planning their visit.

. No pitches. No panels. No crowded rooms. Just you, someone from our team, one coffee and a real conversation.Who it's forAnyone who holds a Web3 domain on any chain:.eth,.sns and.sol,.bnb,.arb and more. Founders, developers, creators, community leads, collectors. If your name lives onchain, there's a seat for you.What we can talk aboutWhat you're building, and how your Web3 name fits into it

Honest feedback on Endless: what works, what's missing, what you'd changeMultichain identity, ENSv2, the.sol upgrade

, or any naming question on your mindPartnerships, integrations and our affiliate program for creators and communitiesLocation & format

Mumbai, India, around the Devcon Week venues.There's no single venue and no group gathering. You book a slot, and a member of the Endless team meets you at a public café nearby.

Each coffee runs about 30 minutes

, the right length to fit between talks.Here's how it worksRSVP: free, and every registration is reviewed. Add your Web3 domain name and a line about what you'd like to talk about.

Quick verification

### About the event

Monad Blitz Mumbai is a one-day hackathon during Devcon week on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. Monad Foundation, Kartikey Garg and The DeDen host the event. Luma lists the event from 09:00 IST on November 4 until midnight at the start of November 5. Experienced EVM developers and people building on Monad for the first time are welcome.

### Building and submissions

The day begins with workshops and practical guidance on Monad, an EVM-compatible Layer 1 blockchain. Teams then work in the hacking area to turn an idea into a functioning prototype, with mentors available for hands-on help. The published sequence finishes with project submissions, MVP demonstrations and recognition of the winning teams. Food breaks and time to talk with other developers, founders, investors and creators are also part of the planned day.

Every hackathon submission must come from a team of two or three members. Projects must be built on Monad; the organizer does not prescribe a product category. Teams compete for a share of a US$5,000 prize pool, which is an award opportunity rather than a payment to every participant.

### Registration options

The organizer offers separate free application categories for Hackathon Registrations, General Admission and Content Creators. General admission is intended for founders, investors and other visitors meeting builders and viewing projects; the creator category is for people covering the event and its projects. All three categories require approval, and capacity is limited. The exact Mumbai venue is shared through registration.

The organizer states that photography, livestreaming and audio or video recording may take place, and that attendance constitutes consent to recording and use of that material under its published event terms.

### Stark Space is coming to Mumbai!

Explore what's being built on Starknet, and meet the people building it.

Taking over one of Mumbai's most iconic restaurants, just a short walk from the main Devcon venue, Stark Space will be a place to plug in throughout the day.

### What to expect

Stark Space brings together builders, founders, developers and people looking to build with, contribute to or explore Starknet.

Start the day with programming - hear from the teams and builders shaping what's next for the network, from Bitcoin and privacy to post-quantum security. Meet the Starknet Foundation team, discover Starknet-native apps and connect directly with the projects behind them.

After programming, the space opens up into Stark Cafe. Grab a seat, start a conversation, or find a quiet corner to work - no agenda, no pressure.

The event is first-come-first-served with limited capacity - we recommend arriving as early as possible so you don't miss out!

### About Starknet

Starknet is a verifiable computer built to expand what products can do onchain. Built on proofs, it gives founders and developers more freedom to keep their products' defining logic onchain, with code written in Cairo and independent verification of execution powered by STARK proofs. Starknet operates as a validity rollup on Ethereum, which provides settlement. Its purpose is to enable a true peer-to-peer economy.

- Record: `ibw-wprc-kol-261104-at-monad-blitz-devcon`
- Source: [ibw-side-events.json](sources/ibw-side-events.json)

### About the event

Multiple Concurrent Proposers + The Rise of PropAMMs1. Cadence Extreme PipeliningCadence redesigns BFT block production by replacing a single leader with multiple proposers running in parallel. Each slot reaches consensus independently, so it does not wait for earlier blocks or network delays. It is built on two parts:

Chorus

, a fast 3-round consensus protocol, and

Conductor

, which controls when new slots open. Cadence provides short-term censorship resistance, hides proposals until they are revealed, and keeps the same security (3f+1 validators) and low latency as single-leader systems. In simulations on Monad's 200-validator network with 5 proposers per slot, it achieved

219 ms

average finality (

167 ms

speculative) and

50 ms

average transaction wait time with

100 ms

block intervals.This is part of Monad Blitz:

https://luma.com/Blitz-Mumbai-Devcon-20262. How Market Makers Are Reshaping Cross-Chain LiquidityTraditional AMMs, such as Uniswap, allow anyone to provide liquidity and earn trading fees. However, their prices typically update only when trades occur, leaving liquidity providers exposed to arbitrageurs who profit from outdated prices.A new model,

proprietary automated market makers (propAMMs)

, is changing this. Unlike traditional AMMs, propAMMs actively update prices without waiting for trades, allowing them to respond faster to market movements. By 2026, propAMMs accounted for more than half of SOL/USDC trading volume on Solana. The paper

:

Active Liquidity On Chain: Evidence from PropAMMs Across Chains

(September 2026), was written by

Ozan Solmaz

(ETH Zurich),

Lioba Heimbach

(Category Labs),

Jason Milionis

(Category Labs)Source:

https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.38056FormatShort introduction and context setting to start.A short walkthrough of the paper and its key ideas.Questions and discussion grounded in the original source.Moderator-led discussion with no promotions. Session Guides:Rongxin Zhang

is the founder of Whitepaper Reading Club (WPRC). Previously, he lead Product at Cobo Custody, CKB, and was part of the founding team of Retsly, acquired by Zillow in 2015. He worked on decentarlized file storage research at Cornell Tech in 2017. Monad FoundationMonad is an institutional-grade blockchain built to power an open, global economy, enabling efficient money movement, tokenization, capital markets, and other financial applications. Built by a team from Jump Crypto.Thank you Elton, and the team for always hosting us!!

About Whitepaper Reading ClubWe are a community of founders, researchers, and builders across Singapore, Malaysia, San Francisco, Bangkok, New York, Lagos, Taipei, and Hong Kong. We meet in person every month to read, discuss, and pressure-test the latest blockchain papers, protocols, and technical ideas.

Website

Summaries

We are ecosystem-agnostic, not for profit, and focused on projects with technical, product, or social innovation.

### About the event

Trilegal and Fractional host the Digital Asset Regulation, Policy and Global Compliance Roundtable in Mumbai on November 4, 2026, from 16:00 to 18:30 IST. The event is for digital-asset founders and operators, general counsel, in-house compliance leads, and legal, regulatory and tax practitioners. Attendees are invited to contribute to the discussion.

### Discussion areas

The first part examines India's current legal and tax treatment of digital assets, including stablecoins, tokenization and FIU registration, with a focus on what these developments mean for businesses and their advisers.

A comparative discussion looks at compliance regimes in the United States, European Union and Singapore, particularly their treatment of stablecoins and tokenized assets. Participants will consider how India's approach compares with those markets.

The final policy discussion asks what a suitable Indian regulatory and tax framework could look like: whether a single dedicated regulator is needed or existing regulators can take responsibility, whether withholding tax is essential, and what role GIFT City should play. The hosts place the conversation in the context of renewed debate about industry self-regulation.

### Schedule and venue

- 16:00 to 16:30 IST: welcome and registration.
- 16:30 to 17:45: roundtable discussion.
- 17:45 to 18:30: mixer.

The organizer's event-specific directions specify the 7th floor, Tower 2A, One World Centre, Lower Parel, Mumbai. This differs from the generic Trilegal map listing's 10th-floor office address. Registration is free and requires host approval.

Trilegal is a law firm advising on matters including fintech, digital assets and regulatory policy. Fractional provides emerging-technology businesses with legal, finance, strategy, technology and operating support.

### About the event

ArQ and Abhiraj Mengade host Diyas: NEAR @Devcon in Mumbai on November 4, 2026, from 16:00 to 20:00 IST. The Diwali-themed gathering uses a team game to demonstrate NEAR cross-chain intents, with participants playing the roles of chains, swaps and confidential transactions.

Before arrival, NEAR AI uses each attendee's RSVP answers to create a physical persona card with a custom animated face and fragments of an intent. Participants find five other people and combine their fragments into a valid cross-chain instruction. The organizer's example is a confidential swap from NEAR to Solana.

The completed instruction goes to an Executor Booth, where an operator executes a US$1 to US$2 onchain micro-intent, with a testnet fallback, and prints the transaction hash. The group receives a Polaroid with the hash and a trusted execution environment (TEE) attestation on the back. That proof can be exchanged at the desk for Diwali merchandise offered as a game reward rather than for sale.

Attendees should complete the RSVP questionnaire and bring a phone and wallet handle. Solo participants can form groups at the door. Registration is free and requires host approval. The organizer describes a Mumbai workspace and rooftop setting; the public location listing identifies Mumbai without a specific street address.

### About the event

EVA Research hosts the EVA Symposium III in Mumbai on Monday, November 2, 2026, from 10:00 to 16:00 IST during Devcon week. The formal academic and research symposium gathers leading cryptographers, computer scientists, and zero-knowledge researchers.

### What to expect

The full-day symposium features peer-reviewed paper presentations, invited keynotes, and technical whiteboard panels:

- Formal verification of smart contracts and consensus state transition systems.
- Zero-Knowledge Virtual Machines (zkVMs): comparing proof recursion, lookup arguments, and constraint system efficiency.
- Cryptographic primitives for verifiable computation, polynomial commitments, and folding schemes.
- Open whiteboard workshops where researchers collaborate on unsolved problems in protocol security.

A catered luncheon and coffee breaks provide ample networking time between sessions.

### Who should attend

The symposium is aimed at cryptography researchers, computer science faculty and graduate students, formal verification engineers, and zero-knowledge protocol architects.

### Venue and schedule

The symposium takes place at a conference auditorium in Mumbai on Monday, November 2, from 10:00 to 16:00 IST.

### Registration and admission

Attendance is free with registration approval required. Applicants are asked to share their academic affiliation, research papers, or GitHub profiles when requesting admission.

### About the event

Cafe Compute Meetup: Mumbai | Devcon Week Edition

Cerebras is excited to present Cafe Compute Meetup in Mumbai during Devcon week, hosted by Cerebras Ambassador Aniket Sahu (https://linkedin.com/in/aniketsahu115) and Arun Chandel (https://www.linkedin.com/in/arun-pratap-singh-chandel-7aa101259/)

Devcon, the Ethereum ecosystem's annual flagship conference, is bringing thousands of developers, founders, researchers and builders from around the world to Mumbai. While the city is buzzing with ideas, take a break from the conference halls and join us for a relaxed evening of fast inference, good food and great conversations about building at the intersection of AI and Web3.

Whether you are in town for Devcon or a Mumbai local and whether you are deep into AI coding tools or just getting started, this is a space to explore ideas, try new workflows and connect with builders from across the world.

### What to Expect

Meet Builders from Around the World

Connect with developers, founders, researchers and AI enthusiasts in Mumbai for Devcon week. Swap stories from the conference, share what you are building and find your next collaborator.

Explore AI Tools and Workflows

Discover Cerebras Inference, OpenAI Codex and open-source AI models. See how fast inference can power AI agents, smart contract tooling, onchain data analysis and the next generation of dApps.

Build, Experiment and Collaborate

Bring your laptop and hack on an idea from the conference, experiment with a new tool or prototype something at the intersection of AI and crypto. Learn from others and build together in a relaxed setting.

Community Show and Tell

Working on something interesting, whether it's an AI agent, a Web3 project, or a developer workflow? Share it with the room, get feedback, and find inspiration for your next build.

Conversations Over Chai

Mumbai is India's financial capital, a city where conversations about markets, trading and the next big idea happen over chai. Join the conversation on how AI and Web3 are reshaping finance, building, and the way we work.

What to Bring

- Your laptop and charger
- A project idea, or something that sparked your curiosity at Devcon
- Your curiosity and enthusiasm for building with AI

Event Flow

- 6:30 PM: Doors open, check-in, and welcome
- 7:00 PM: Welcome to Cafe Compute, Devcon Week Edition
- 7:35 PM: Exploring Cerebras, Codex, and AI development workflows
- 7:50 PM: Hands-on exploration, building, and collaboration
- 8:35 PM: Community show and tell
- 8:55 PM: Open discussion on AI x Web3, ideas, and experiences
- 9:15 PM: Community conversations and wrap-up
- 9:30 PM: Event ends

### About Cerebras

Cerebras builds some of the world's fastest AI inference systems, powered by its Wafer-Scale Engine technology. Cerebras Inference enables developers to run AI models at high speeds and explore new possibilities for AI-powered applications.

Explore Cerebras Inference and available models at Cerebras.ai (https://Cerebras.ai).

Join the Community (https://chat.whatsapp.com/JFJAkHciDFs3y3uLRES7Zf?s=cl&p=i&ilr=4&iam=2)

Cafe Compute is about bringing people together to explore, experiment and build with AI. Whether you are an experienced developer or just starting your journey, come share ideas, discover new tools and connect with others who are excited about what AI makes possible.

Bring your laptop, grab something to eat and let's build together!

Cerebras is the world's fastest AI inference, up to 15x faster than leading GPUs. Cerebras Inference is powered by our Wafer-Scale Engine (WSE-3) - the world's largest AI chip. Experience the speed for yourself with OpenAI Codex-Spark, powered on Cerebras, or one of the open source models like Qwen 3.8 28B. Get free compute at Cerebras.ai (https://cerebras.ai).

- Premium open bar and passed hors d'oeuvres in an upscale setting designed for high-level relationship building.

### Who should attend

This gathering is curated for institutional investors, family office directors, asset managers, fintech executives, crypto custody specialists, and DeFi protocol founders.

### Venue and schedule

The mixer is hosted in the Bandra Kurla Complex (BKC), Mumbai, on Wednesday night, November 4, from 21:00 to 23:30 IST.

### Registration and admission

Registration is free of charge and requires approval. Professional credentials or fund affiliations must be provided during RSVP to ensure a curated guest list.

### About the event

Your node can stay online without you for 45 minutes. Probably.

One free, easy-paced 45-minute waterfront walk where you can actually hear the person next to you. Come solo - no stage, speeches, sales pitches or forced introductions.

### Who should join?

Ethereum client developers, node operators, RPC teams, infra founders and L2 researchers. People of all genders and experience levels are welcome.

### What you'll get

Meet the people behind invisible infrastructure, and talk about hard problems without a panel.

Conversation starter, if you want one: What infra issue deserves much more attention?

### When, where and how to find us

- Date: Thursday, 5 November 2026
- Walk: 7:00-7:45 AM IST. Arrive by 6:50 AM to meet the group before we move.
- Meeting landmark: Carter Road Amphitheatre, 3 Sherly Rajan Road, Bandra West, Mumbai 400050. Use the map pin on this Luma page, not the Devcon venue.
- Exact entrance and route: The precise side of the landmark and safe public pedestrian path will be confirmed in an event update before the walk, after local access checks. Please check your Luma updates.
- Format: Easy walk, optional gentle jog. No fitness requirements. Bring water, comfortable shoes and a charged phone.

### RSVP and ticket

This walk is FREE, and registration has no fixed attendee cap. A valid Devcon 8 ticket is required for participation. Your RSVP does not include a Devcon ticket. You only need to confirm ticket ownership in the form - never send your ticket QR code.

Safety: We stay on accessible public pedestrian areas; no traffic-road running, risky shorelines or pressure to match others' pace. Weather or access checks may require a change or cancellation, communicated to registered guests through Luma.

Independently hosted by Veerendra Vamshi, founder of Proof of Audits. Not officially endorsed by Devcon or the Ethereum Foundation.

## Frontier Of Intelligence Hackathon

- Record: `india-luma-ub56pe38`
- Source: [ibw-side-events.json](sources/ibw-side-events.json)
- Starts: 2026-11-05T03:30:00.000Z
- Description: Source-backed
- Original page: <https://luma.com/ub56pe38>

### About the event

Frontier of Intelligence Hackathon brings developers, founders, researchers and designers working on AI, Web3 and autonomous systems to Mumbai from November 5, 2026, at 09:00 IST to November 6 at 17:00 IST. Hosted by Lakshmi, it offers mentorship in AI, cryptography and protocol design, alongside infrastructure partners for compute, LLM tooling and Web3 development. The organizer also describes routes to accelerator, grant and venture-capital opportunities.

### Technical tracks

- Autonomous AI Agents and Multi-Agent Systems: This track covers agents that coordinate onchain, execute financial or governance actions, interact with smart contracts and collaborate with other agents. It emphasizes agent economies, agent-to-agent commerce and onchain execution layers.
- Decentralized AI Infrastructure: Projects can address decentralized compute markets, verifiable inference, zero-knowledge machine learning (ZK-ML), distributed training or model marketplaces.
- Intelligence for Real-World Systems: Applications include healthcare AI infrastructure, climate coordination, financial intelligence, defense and cyber coordination, and autonomous supply chains.

### Announced awards

The US$5,000 grand prize is for the most impactful project across the tracks, assessed on technical depth, originality, real-world potential and scalability. Track winners are offered US$3,000 each. A separate US$2,000 Frontier Research Prize covers experimental, research-grade work such as ZK-ML, new coordination mechanisms, agent-to-agent economic systems and novel protocol design. These are competitive awards for selected projects; accelerator, grant and investor connections are opportunities rather than guaranteed funding for participants.

Registration is free and requires host approval. The exact Mumbai venue is private and available through registration.

### About the event

IMPORTANT: Access to the hub is only for Devcon ticket holders. Get yours here. (https://devcon.org/en/tickets/)

Privacy gives you the freedom to act on your own terms. Join us at the Practical Privacy Day to meet the builders working on privacy across Ethereum and beyond, and learn how you can take more control over your data.

You'll hear how teams are bringing privacy to Ethereum's L1 and explore different approaches to privacy-centric L2s. See open-source hardware wallets in action and learn how to prepare for a post-quantum future. We'll explore practical tools you can use day-to-day, from VPNs, AI tools that respect your data, to open-source alternatives.

The day is designed for anyone and everyone interested in on and offchain privacy solutions. No technical knowledge required.

10:00 - 10:30 | Privacy 101: What is Privacy and Why Should You Care | Kyle (https://x.com/PryvitKyle) (Brave)

### About the event

Deepflow and Eureka Labs host the Onchain Execution Dinner in Mumbai on Thursday, November 5, 2026, from 19:00 to 22:00 IST during Devcon week. The technical dinner convenes virtual machine architects, compiler engineers, and core protocol researchers.

### What to expect

The dinner is structured around technical whiteboard discussions and peer presentations:

- Parallel execution architectures, multi-threaded virtual machines, and optimistic concurrency control in high-throughput rollups.
- State access optimization, flat databases, and memory-mapped state storage for sub-second block times.
- JIT compilation, eBPF runtimes, and bytecode verification improvements for next-generation EVM and SVM environments.
- Multi-course dining with wine and beer, providing ample time for technical debates and collaboration.

### Who should attend

The dinner is curated for systems programmers, compiler engineers, virtual machine researchers, Layer 1/Layer 2 core developers, and performance optimization specialists.

### Venue and schedule

The dinner takes place at an upscale private dining venue in the Bandra Kurla Complex (BKC), Mumbai, on Thursday, November 5, from 19:00 to 22:00 IST.

### Registration and admission

Registration is strictly approval-based with limited seating. Applications are reviewed based on engineering background and contributions to execution layer research. Approved guests receive confirmation and venue details.

## Clear-Signing & Wallet Security @ DEVCON

- Record: `ibw-luma-evt-7bLYYfCCvXDasQt`
- Source: [ibw-side-events.json](sources/ibw-side-events.json)
- Starts: 2026-11-07T06:30:00.000Z
- Description: Source-backed
- Original page: <https://luma.com/kwi8jlpk>

### About the event

The ERC-8009 team is hosting an event dedicated to clear signing and ways to achieve it.

The existing and experimental solutions will be demonstrated using Ledger and Trezor devices.

Clear signing is a solution to Blind Signing, which is the single biggest security threat currently facing everyday Web3 users and protocol teams. It occurs when a hardware wallet cannot decode the transaction and present it in human language, so the end user approving the wallet transaction is left guessing whether the transaction is exactly what they intend to send. In many cases, unsuspecting users simply approve such transactions, accepting the risk.

Even though hardware wallets are commonly thought of as the ultimate security solution, they are still prone to attacks involving "blind signing". For example, that's exactly what happened to Bybit when the Safe code was modified and the hardware wallet couldn't provide a human-language explanation of the transaction (the famous $1.5B hack).

Join us during DEVCON Mumbai 2026 for a practical session exploring Clear-Signing solutions, amongst which ERC-8009 (Proxy Clear Signing) will be presented, with demos on real hardware devices.

- Record: `ibw-luma-evt-QkWwyZht8EIQiUy`
- Source: [ibw-side-events.json](sources/ibw-side-events.json)

### About the event

The conference ends. The conversations don't have to.

One free, easy-paced 45-minute waterfront walk where you can actually hear the person next to you. Come solo - no stage, speeches, sales pitches or forced introductions.

### Who should join?

Devcon builders, auditors, founders, DeFi users, creators and anyone wanting a relaxed farewell. People of all genders and experience levels are welcome.

### What you'll get

Close out conference week with real conversation and people worth following up with.

Conversation starter, if you want one: Who would you like to keep talking with after Mumbai?

### When, where and how to find us

- Date: Saturday, 7 November 2026
- Walk: 7:30-8:15 PM IST. Arrive by 7:20 PM to meet the group before we move.
- Meeting landmark: Carter Road Amphitheatre, 3 Sherly Rajan Road, Bandra West, Mumbai 400050. Use the map pin on this Luma page, not the Devcon venue.
- Exact entrance and route: The precise side of the landmark and safe public pedestrian path will be confirmed in an event update before the walk, after local access checks. Please check your Luma updates.
- Format: Easy walk, optional gentle jog. No fitness requirements. Bring water, comfortable shoes and a charged phone.

### RSVP and ticket

This walk is FREE, and registration has no fixed attendee cap. A valid Devcon 8 ticket is required for participation. Your RSVP does not include a Devcon ticket. You only need to confirm ticket ownership in the form - never send your ticket QR code.

Safety: We stay on accessible public pedestrian areas; no traffic-road running, risky shorelines or pressure to match others' pace. Weather or access checks may require a change or cancellation, communicated to registered guests through Luma.

Independently hosted by Veerendra Vamshi, founder of Proof of Audits. Not officially endorsed by Devcon or the Ethereum Foundation.

## Bitshala BOSS Summit 2026 \| Jaipur \| 26 Oct - 31 Oct

- Record: `india-luma-bitshalaboss`
- Source: [india-luma-events.json](sources/india-luma-events.json)

- Description: Source-backed
- Original page: <https://luma.com/bitshalaboss>

### Bitshala BOSS (Bitcoin Open-Source Software) Summit 2026 | Jaipur

Join us for 6 days of fun, work, collaboration, and deep learning at the frontiers of Bitcoin open-source software design and development.

### What's happening

Expect a highly collaborative residency with sessions, workshops, demos, open discussions, and hands-on building time.

You'll get to:

- Learn what's happening at the frontiers of Bitcoin OSS development and design
- Meet developers and designers working on active Bitcoin projects
- Connect with product builders and educators taking Bitcoin to more people
- Share demos, prototypes, workshops, and project ideas
- Find collaborators for GitHub repos, Figma files, personal projects, or products
- Spend time with fellow builders through games, sports, bonfires, walks, treks, and sightseeing

Whether you're contributing to open-source software, designing better Bitcoin user experiences, building educational content, or working on a product, BOSS Summit is designed to help you meet the right people and move your work forward.

### Timelines

- Monday, 26 Oct
  - Check-in
  - 16:00 : Welcome & introductions
- Tuesday, 27 Oct - Thursday, 29 Oct (10:00 - 17:00)
  - Sessions, Workshops, Open Slots, Demos, Project discussions and Collaboration time
  - Evenings will include fun games, sports, bonfires, and informal hangouts.
- Friday, 30 Oct - Saturday, 31 Oct
  - Bitmela
- Sunday, 1 Nov
  - Checkout by 11:00 AM

### Who Should Apply

We have limited seats for:

- Bitcoin developers
- Product designers
- UX/UI designers
- Bitcoin educators
- Product builders
- People actively working on Bitcoin projects, tools, content, or education

Seats are sponsored by Bitshala, so please make a strong application to help us understand what you're working on and how you hope to contribute during the residency.

### Bring Your Work

Have an active GitHub repo, a Figma file, a workshop idea, a product prototype, or a personal project?

Bring it along.

BOSS Summit is a place to share work-in-progress, find collaborators, get feedback, jam on ideas, and build alongside others who care deeply about Bitcoin and open-source software.

### Bringing a Family Member or Friend

If you're planning to bring a family member or friend, we'll connect you with the venue provider or Airbnb options.

You can directly pay for their stay and meals with the provider.

### Apply to Get Invited

BOSS Summit has limited invited seats for Bitcoin developers, designers, educators, and builders.

If you're excited to learn, contribute, build, teach, design, or collaborate around Bitcoin open-source software, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply now and tell us what you're building.

For any queries drop a mail to contact@bitshala.org

### Glimpse of Our Last BOSS Summit

Dharmshala - Summer 2026

Catch a glimpse of the energy, collaboration, and moments from our last BOSS Summit in Dharmshala - from deep work sessions and demos to bonfires, games, and community bonding.

Explore [more here: The official BOSS Summit After-Movie and Article](https://x.com/bitshala_org/status/2049831566827008161)

### About Bitshala

[Bitshala](https://bitshala.org/) is a Bitcoin-focused education initiative where we help developers, designers, and curious builders learn by doing. We run cohorts, clubs, workshops, a hackerspace, and community programs that make it easier for people to explore, contribute to, and build on Bitcoin. Our focus is on hands-on learning, proof-of-work, and growing alongside a community of people who care about open technology, design, and the future of money.

If you'd like to explore more, check us out on:

- Discord (Online Community) (https://discord.com/invite/STeQFVEWf9)
- [Cohort registration and fellowship application portal](https://app.bitshala.org/)
- Twitter (Socials and Announcements) (https://x.com/bitshala_org)
- Luma (Events Calendar) (https://luma.com/bitshala)

## Navigating Career Transitions in the Age of AI: Defining Your Professional Narrative

### About the event

As technology rapidly reshapes industries, job roles, and required skill sets, professionals are increasingly being asked to adapt before the path forward is fully clear. Whether navigating a career transition, responding to AI-driven disruption, repositioning yourself in a competitive job market, or hiring talent for emerging roles, success depends on more than technical expertise - it requires the ability to tell a compelling professional story.

This highly interactive session uses Interactive Business Theater, featuring professional actors portraying realistic workplace and career conversations, to explore how individuals can define and communicate their unique value in a changing world of work. Through facilitated discussion, audience participation, and practical frameworks, participants will learn how to build a professional narrative that aligns their experiences, strengths, and aspirations with evolving employer needs.

Learning Objectives:

- Identify and articulate your unique value proposition in a rapidly evolving labor market
- Translate past experiences and transferable skills into a compelling professional narrative
- Position yourself competitively amid AI, automation, and shifting workforce demands
- Navigate career development conversations with greater confidence, clarity, and adaptability

Facilitator: Rahul Kay, MBA, MPH

Rahul Kay helps organizations develop leaders who can navigate uncertainty, drive performance, and build stronger workplace cultures. As the Director of Client Success, his work focuses on leadership development, organizational effectiveness, and experiential learning. Prior to Ibis, Rahul was the CEO of an employee mental health organization, worked in organizational strategy at McKinsey, and supported change initiatives through the United Nations. He holds an MBA from the MIT Sloan School of Management, and MPH from Tufts Medical, and studied clinical psychology at Cornell.

## Maritime Dual-Use Hackathon

- Record: `luma-crypto-T8jvG7h5xieJmQL`
- Source: [luma-crypto-events.json](sources/luma-crypto-events.json)
- Starts: 2026-10-16T23:30:00.000Z
- Description: Source-backed
- Original page: <https://luma.com/mvcg9eyw>

### About the event

The Fincantieri Maritime Dual-Use Hackathon comes to San Francisco, October 16-18.

Following the first edition in Rome, which brought together 70+ participants, including Italian Navy engineers, and produced five working prototypes, the challenge now crosses the Atlantic to the Bay Area's deep-tech ecosystem.

Over 48 hours, engineers, developers, founders, researchers and designers will form teams to build working solutions around real maritime and defense engineering challenges, with access to technical mentors, development hardware and potential opportunities to continue developing the strongest concepts beyond the event.

### Challenge Tracks

1. OT Cybersecurity & Blast Radius Analysis
2. Piping Layout Optimization
3. Software-Defined Vessel

### Build with Real Hardware

Participants will have access to a selection of Qualcomm and Arduino technologies during the hackathon, including Snapdragon-powered laptops, edge AI and robotics development platforms, Arduino prototyping hardware and supporting developer tools.

These tools are intended for hands-on technical development. Participants with experience in areas such as software development, embedded systems, electronics, robotics, edge AI, computer vision or hardware prototyping will be best positioned to take full advantage of them.

Qualcomm and Arduino technologies will be introduced during the opening session so teams can quickly understand the available resources and integrate hardware, edge AI, computer vision, sensors or robotics into their prototypes.

Exact hardware configurations will be shared with participants ahead of the event.

### More Than a 48-Hour Hackathon

The goal is not only to build a prototype, but to identify ideas with the potential to continue developing after the event.

- Work on real Fincantieri challenges with potential relevance to future maritime and defense applications.
- Compete for a Qualcomm-powered laptop awarded to the winning team.
- Develop your concept beyond the hackathon: selected promising prototypes may have the opportunity to continue evolving.
- Access Fincantieri expertise: winning and particularly promising concepts may receive mentoring from Fincantieri's network of experts to help further mature the solution and explore its potential application within Fincantieri.
- Connect with leading technical talent from industry, academia, venture capital and the defense innovation ecosystem.

### Partners & Ecosystem

[The hackathon is powered by Fincantieri](https://www.fincantieri.com/en), [Mind The Bridge](https://mindthebridge.com/)[and Silicon Mountain](https://www.linkedin.com/company/silicon-mtn/posts/?feedView=all).

Qualcomm is the main technology sponsor, supporting participants with hardware, development resources and technology expertise throughout the event.

Additional experts from Fincantieri, academia, industry, venture capital and the defense innovation ecosystem will support teams through mentoring and judging.

### What to Expect

- 48 hours of hands-on building and prototyping
- Real technical challenges provided by Fincantieri
- Access to Qualcomm and Arduino hardware and development resources
- Mentors and domain experts supporting teams throughout the event
- Collaboration with engineers, founders, and researchers
- A Qualcomm-powered laptop prize for the winning team
- Potential follow-on development opportunities for the most promising concepts

No maritime background is required. However, this is a hands-on technical hackathon, and participants should be ready to contribute directly through software development, AI/ML, embedded systems, cybersecurity, robotics, engineering, CAD/optimization, product design or prototyping.

Come with a team or find one at the event.

### About the event

NOTE: By registering for the Luma, you are submitting an application to participate. We will reach out on a rolling basis to let you know whether you've been accepted. There are a limited number of devices, we can support up to 200 participants.

This event is sponsored by Meta, Qualcomm, GitHub, Open Intelligence Foundation, and the PyTorch Foundation.

Join developers, researchers, and builders for the upcoming ExecuTorch Hackathon on October 17 -18 at [Founder's Inc., officially part of Open Source AI Week 2026](https://opensourceaiweek.com/).

[Hosted in collaboration with Qualcomm](https://www.qualcomm.com/developer), [Meta](https://www.meta.com/), [GitHub](https://github.com/), [the PyTorch Foundation](https://pytorch.org/foundation/), [and Open Intelligence Foundation](https://openintelligence.foundation/), this hands-on event will challenge teams [to build innovative AI experiences powered by ExecuTorch](https://executorch.ai/) - an open-source framework for deploying and running PyTorch models efficiently on edge and on-device hardware.

Participants will work in teams of 3-5 people and select one of three tracks outlined below. Each team will receive a device from their selected track to use during the event. Builders will also get access to GitHub Copilot Pro+ to support their builds.

Compute Track

Build AI applications optimized for the Copilot+ PC powered by Snapdragon® X Elite processors, exploring the potential of powerful, efficient on-device AI computing.

Mobile + XR Track

Create AI-powered experiences for the Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra powered by Snapdragon 8 Elite and Samsung Galaxy XR powered by Snapdragon® XR2+ Gen 2 processor, with a focus on mobile intelligence, immersive interaction, and multimodal applications.

IoT Track

Develop intelligent edge and embedded applications using the Arduino® VENTUNO™ Q boards, combining on-device AI with real-time sensing, control, and connected experiences. Choose from an assortment of modulinos and accessories to complete your project (available on a first come, first served basis).

To participate, interested teams must select a track, form a team of 3-5, and submit a project proposal by October 4. Selected teams will be announced by October 7.

### Prizes

The top team in each track will receive a prize package for every member of the team: Meta AI glasses and an Arduino® UNO™ Q. Build a standout project, demonstrate the potential of on-device AI, and take home hardware to continue exploring the edge.

GitHub will also award a one-year subscription to Copilot Pro to the winner.

Whether you are an experienced edge AI developer or eager to explore the future of open-source, on-device intelligence, the ExecuTorch Hackathon is an opportunity to collaborate, experiment, and build with the latest hardware and software across compute, mobile, XR, and IoT.

Questions? Join our Discord!

Ask questions about the event, connect with other participants, form a team, receive event announcements, and stay up to date throughout the hackathon.

Join here: https://discord.gg/A635v4hMSg

Bring your ideas. Build with ExecuTorch. Help shape the future of open-source, on device AI.

### About Open Intelligence Foundation

[The Open Intelligence Foundation](https://openintelligence.foundation/) is a community-first nonprofit founded to protect, strengthen, and advance open-source AI, open models, and open science. Supported by a large community of volunteers and organizations, it takes a bottom-up approach to collaboration, working with academia and researchers to support research, development, and education in [open-source AI. The foundation also leads Open Source AI Week](https://opensourceaiweek.com/), a community-run initiative celebrating open-source AI.

About Founders, Inc.

[Founders, Inc.](https://f.inc/) backs early-stage founders in emerging tech with first checks and 55,000 sq. ft. of lab space in San Francisco's Fort Mason. They run year-round programs to help ambitious builders to go from early stage to scalable companies.

Snapdragon and Qualcomm branded products are products of Qualcomm Technologies, Inc. and/or its subsidiaries. Arduino and VENTUNO are trademarks or registered trademarks of Arduino S.r.l.

### What's actually working for AI growth right now?

Building an AI product has never been easier. Getting real users, distribution, and revenue is still hard.

Local Align #3 is a hands-on day for people who want to learn how modern AI products actually grow - from SEO/GEO and organic content to developer growth, community, outbound, automation, and AI-powered GTM.

Learn from real growth stories.

Hear founders break down how they went from 0 → 1,000+ users, built communities of 10,000+, and generated millions of organic impressions without relying on paid acquisition.

Put it into practice.

Choose from 5 real products with 5 different GTM problems - AI DevTools, consumer community, high-trust services, FinTech, and generative AI - and use AI, code, content, or automation to move real metrics: users, leads, signups, traffic, and conversions.

Meet the people building around you.

Not hacking? Come for the talks, startup demos, Coffee Chats, board games, food, and an afternoon with founders, engineers, creators, students, and GTM operators from across the Bay Area.

Come to learn. Come to build. Come to meet your next collaborator, customer, cofounder - or simply someone worth knowing.

You do not need to compete to attend.

### Learn: How Products Actually Grow

No generic startup advice. Hear real 0→1 growth stories from founders and operators who have built audiences, acquired users, and turned distribution into a system.

Lucy Ye - Co-founder & COO, JobWizard.ai (https://JobWizard.ai)

SEO/GEO × Organic Content × AI-Native Growth

Built a 0→1 SEO engine that generated 2M+ Google Search impressions in 2 months, plus 1M+ organic video impressions with zero paid acquisition. Learn how an early-stage AI startup turns search, content, and AI automation into repeatable distribution.

Weijia - Founder & CEO, LingCode

Developer Growth × Product-Led Growth × Community

Built content reaching millions, grew a coding education platform from 0 → 10,000+ students, and took LingCode from launch to 1,000+ users in its first month. Learn how technical founders can turn product, content, and community into an organic growth engine.

More founders & GTM operators to be announced.

### Build: 5 Real Products. 5 Real Growth Problems

Most hackathons ask you to build another demo.

Here, you'll work on a real product with real users and a real GTM problem - then use AI, code, content, outbound, SEO/GEO, automation, communities, or whatever else you can invent to move the numbers.

AI Developer Tools - LingCode

How do you win developers when every week brings another AI coding tool?

Grow an AI-native IDE through developer communities, technical content, product-led loops, GEO, creators, or your own growth automation.

Learn: developer GTM, PLG, community growth, and how technical products earn adoption.

Consumer Community - Tennistry

3,500+ users. 1,500+ real tennis matches. How do you create the next 1,000?

Tennistry connects tennis players in real life. Test local acquisition, referrals, ambassadors, events, creators, and ways to prove which users you actually brought in.

Learn: consumer growth, network effects, referral loops, local/community GTM, and attribution.

🇺🇸 High-Trust Services - TurboNIW

How do you acquire customers when the decision is expensive, complex, and built on trust?

TurboNIW helps STEM researchers and professionals prepare for the EB-2 NIW process through structured educational materials and guidance. Unlike with a casual app download, customers may spend $1,000+ and are making a high-stakes career decision - making trust and intent central to acquisition. TurboNIW (https://www.turboniw.com/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

Learn: high-intent SEO/GEO, trust-based funnels, educational content, lead qualification, and customer acquisition for high-consideration services.

Consumer FinTech - MaxWorth

30,000 users already. What becomes the next scalable growth channel?

MaxWorth is a North American credit-card management app entering its next stage of growth. Explore finance content, SEO/GEO, creators, referrals, communities, partnerships, or new product-led acquisition loops.

Learn: consumer FinTech GTM, lifecycle growth, referral mechanics, content distribution, and scaling beyond early adopters.

Generative AI × Entertainment - SxeneMixer

A new AI creative product is starting from zero. Where do the first 100 real users come from?

SxeneMixer is an AI short-drama generation platform. Find the creators and communities most likely to care, then experiment with UGC, viral formats, creator seeding, social distribution, and product-led sharing.

Learn: 0→1 launches, creator GTM, UGC, viral loops, and consumer AI distribution.

Pick the problem you want to learn about. Build the growth experiment. Run it on a real product. Show us what happened.

More challenges will be revealed.

### About the event

Car AI Navigation Hackathon

Challenge: We have a mini city road with lanes, an intersection and traffic signs. Your job is to use AI and a small autonomous car like the Donkeycar or equivalent (typically a 1/16th-scale or smaller RC car with a Raspberry Pi or equivalent and a camera controlling it) to navigate the "city", obeying signs and making it from one side to the other in the fastest time.

You must bring your own car, which should be ready to run, with compute and a camera already onboard and working. The objective of the hackathon is to add AI "city" navigation to it.

You can use onboard AI, AI on your laptop via Wifi or AI in the cloud to help with the navigation. Think creatively about what kind of AI to use and what the fastest way to do it is!

This is not an event for spectators, nor will cars be provided to those who arrive without one. This is a hackathon, not a regular race. Come ready to hack!

### Bitcoin India Tour - IIT Goa Edition

Bitcoin India Tour is a nationwide educational initiative bringing Bitcoin education to students across India. The tour explores the evolution of money, the problems with existing monetary systems, and the technology behind Bitcoin from first principles.

The IIT Goa Edition at the Indian Institute of Technology Goa brings an engaging learning experience for students interested in technology, computer science, economics, finance, and the future of money.

Starting with the fundamentals of money and moving into the technology behind Bitcoin, this session is designed to help students understand why Bitcoin was created, how it works, and what makes it different from traditional monetary systems.

### What You'll Learn

- The evolution of money and how monetary systems have changed
- Inflation, purchasing power, and the importance of sound money
- Problems with the current monetary system
- What Bitcoin is and why it was created
- Bitcoin's fixed supply and monetary properties
- How the Bitcoin network works
- Bitcoin mining, nodes, blocks, and network security
- Global Bitcoin adoption and real-world use cases
- Opportunities to learn, build, research, and contribute to the Bitcoin ecosystem

### Who Should Attend?

- Engineering and technology students
- Developers and aspiring builders
- Students interested in economics and finance
- Entrepreneurs and innovators
- Anyone curious about Bitcoin and the future of money

No prior knowledge of Bitcoin is required.

### Event Format

Educational Bitcoin session

Interactive presentation and demonstrations

Bitcoin technology and fundamentals

Open discussion

Networking with fellow students and Bitcoin enthusiasts

Q&A session

### About Bitcoin India Tour

Bitcoin India Tour is building a grassroots Bitcoin education movement across Indian campuses, creating opportunities for students to learn about money, understand Bitcoin, ask questions, and connect with like-minded individuals.

Join us at IIT Goa to learn Bitcoin from first principles and explore the ideas and technology shaping the future of money.

## RWA新階段：實物資產如何真正上鏈

- Record: `luma-crypto-gNTVHMUFj01ZOGH`
- Source: [luma-crypto-events.json](sources/luma-crypto-events.json)

### About the event

RWA 新階段：實物資產如何真正上鏈

宏觀週期之下，RWA 的價值重估與落地路徑

適逢 2026 香港金融科技週，國富量子聯合星路 Finloop，邀請來自金融機構、區塊鏈基礎設施與實物資產領域的嘉賓齊聚上環，用一個下午的時間，聊透 RWA 從「概念」走向「落地」的關鍵一步。

隨著香港 RWA 與穩定幣監管框架逐步完善，越來越多實物資產開始嘗試上鏈。但一項資產究竟如何完成確權、結構設計、代幣化發行，並最終進入二級市場流通？本場活動將以亞洲首個加拿大油氣資產通證化項目為案例，從宏觀環境、交易結構、鏈上技術到底層資產，完整拆解實物資產上鏈的全流程。

你將收穫

- 全球宏觀變局下，RWA 賽道的機會與風險判斷
- 一個真實能源資產 RWA 項目的完整結構拆解
- 資產代幣化背後的技術與鏈上基礎設施
- 與機構投資者、項目方及生態夥伴的深度交流

議程安排

- 嘉賓簽到
- 主題分享 01｜宏觀經濟：全球擾動頻發下的宏觀前瞻。主講：李總，中金香港資產管理部副總經理
- 主題分享 02｜RWA 案例：亞洲首個加拿大油氣資產通證化項目全解析。主講：Charles Zeng，國富量子 Global Head of Digital Assets
- 主題分享 03｜上鏈技術：資產代幣化技術與鏈上基礎設施。主講：Colin，星路科技執行董事
- 主題分享 04｜底層資產：油氣項目方解讀底層資產結構
- 圓桌討論：從鏈下資產到鏈上金融：RWA 的價值重塑與落地實踐
 - Jacky Kong｜Head of HK, Ava Labs
 - 王龍｜主席，大灣區金融家協會
 - 阮健 Susie Ruan｜董事總經理、金融產品負責人，EXIO Limited
 - Daisy｜COO，鑰坤科技
 - David Wang ｜Partner, Jun He Law Offices
- 自由交流

## 架构破局，风控筑底｜2026 香港 RWA 与稳定币支付机构闭门峰会

- Record: `luma-crypto-XPHsbcLYGE55yny`

### About the event

RWA 与稳定币支付正从概念探索走向业务落地。随着资产发行、交易分销、支付结算和托管服务逐渐交织，机构在拓展业务的同时，也需要面对合规要求、风控体系、跨境协作与安全应急等现实挑战。

为此，慢雾(SlowMist) 携手君合律师事务所，将于 11 月 2 日在香港举办「架构破局，风控筑底｜2026 香港 RWA 与稳定币支付机构闭门峰会」行业交流活动。

本次闭门峰会将邀请相关领域的机构代表，围绕 RWA 与稳定币支付的商业实践和风险治理展开交流，探讨业务如何落地、机构如何协作，以及如何为快速发展的市场筑牢安全与合规基础。

### 活动信息

活动时间：2026 年 11 月 2 日（星期一）14:00-18:30

活动地点：香港中环友邦金融中心

活动主办：慢雾(SlowMist) 、君合律师事务所

### 活动议程

即将发布

### 主办方信息

慢雾科技 SlowMist

慢雾科技是一家专注区块链生态安全的威胁情报公司，成立于 2018 年 1 月，由一支拥有十多年一线网络安全攻防实战经验的团队创建，团队成员曾打造了拥有世界级影响力的安全工程。慢雾科技已是国际化的区块链安全头部公司，主要提供"由 AI 驱动、从威胁发现到威胁防御一体化、因地制宜"的安全解决方案，服务全球众多头部及知名的项目，已有商业客户上千家，客户分布在十几个主要国家与地区。

慢雾科技积极参与区块链安全行标、国标及国际标准的推进工作，是国内首批进入工信部《2018 年中国区块链产业白皮书》的单位，成立不到两年就获得「国家高新技术企业」认定。慢雾科技在「网络安全精英嘉许计划(CSPA)2025 」中，荣获香港警务处网络安全及科技罪案调查科颁发的"网络安全卓越贡献奖"；旗下反洗钱追踪分析平台 MistTrack ，亦在 HKICT Awards 2025 评选中荣获 FinTech (RegTech: Regulatory and Risk Management) 金奖。慢雾科技在新型加密货币犯罪调查方面有很多积累，研究成果被多个国际组织和政府部门引用，包括但不限于：联合国安理会、联合国毒品与犯罪问题办公室。

慢雾科技的安全解决方案包括：SlowMist AI、安全审计、威胁情报(BTI)、防御部署等服务并配套有加密货币反洗钱追踪分析平台(MistTrack)、面向大型机构的反洗钱合规引擎(SlowMist KYT)、假充值漏洞扫描、Web3 威胁情报与动态安全监测(MistEye)、被黑档案库(SlowMist Hacked) 等 SaaS 型安全产品。基于成熟有效的安全服务及安全产品，慢雾科技联动国际顶级的安全公司，如 Akamai、BitDefender、RC²、天际友盟、IPIP 等及海内外加密货币知名项目方、司法鉴定、执法机构等，从威胁发现到威胁防御上提供了一体化因地制宜的安全解决方案。慢雾科技在行业内曾独立发现并公布数多起通用高风险的区块链安全漏洞，得到业界的广泛关注与认可。给区块链生态带来安全感是慢雾科技努力的方向。

官网：https://www.slowmist.com/

X: https://x.com/SlowMist_Team

君合律师事务所

君合律师事务所于 1989 年创立于北京，是中国最早的合伙制律师事务所之一。发展至今，君合已在海内外拥有十五个办公室和逾千人的专业团队，是国际公认的、卓越的中国大型综合律师事务所之一。

## Ethereum Classic Mumbai

- Record: `luma-crypto-TQDZinnxGDGJiHK`
- Source: [luma-crypto-events.json](sources/luma-crypto-events.json)
- Starts: 2026-11-02T13:30:00.000Z
- Description: Source-backed
- Original page: <https://luma.com/flt0wvtq>

### About the event

Ethereum and Ethereum Classic were once the same chain, until the DAO hard fork in 2016 sent them down separate paths. Ethereum later moved to Proof of Stake, while Classic stayed with Proof of Work. Ten years on, ETC enters its second decade, and every chain now faces new threats from quantum computers and AI.

We're a 15-minute walk from Ethereum Cypherpunk Congress #3 (https://congress.web3privacy.info/), and we invite you to this casual evening after it closes, the night before Devcon 8 opens, to pull up a chair and talk with Ethereum Classic developers and contributors.

### Who It's For

Builders on any EVM chain, node runners and miners, Congress and Devcon people, and anyone curious about Ethereum Classic.

Let's Talk About

We think ETC, the EVM chain with the greatest hash rate, is going to make a comeback.

Quantum computers threaten the elliptic-curve signatures every chain uses today, but ETC's consensus rests on hash-based Proof of Work, which shouldn't need to be migrated. Mining a block takes real hardware and energy, and there are no validator keys to steal or forge. Wallets are a different story, and we still need to figure out post-quantum signatures for ETC accounts, looking to Ethereum's research on this for inspiration.

Coming straight from the Cypherpunk Congress, we also thought it would be interesting to talk about the cypherpunk ideas ETC was built on, like censorship resistance and protocol neutrality, and about EVM symbiosis, since ETC and Ethereum share the EVM and the same contracts, tools and builders can work on both.

We think ETC is an underdog with a bright future, carried through ten years by people who stayed for principles that never die.

### Schedule

- 19:00 Doors open
- 19:30 A short welcome from Classix
- 19:45-22:00 Open discussions

### Venue

Leopold Cafe is a Classic Colaba Causeway landmark since 1871, with food, a full bar and a 15-minute walk from the Congress. Find us upstairs from 7pm.

Space at Leopold Cafe is limited and registrations are high. If we fill up, people in the ETC Mumbai Matrix room get priority, so join #etc-mumbai:matrix.org (https://matrix.to/#/#etc-mumbai:matrix.org) before the night.

Hosted by classix.dev (https://classix.dev)

Come with a real draft, not a concept. You'll leave knowing exactly what to cut and what to sharpen before you hit submit.

### 智能金融・真實資產・全球資本

AI × RWA Investment Forum 2026

從傳統金融到 Web3，從資產價值到全球資本。

由環球數字資本孵化器 (亞太) 有限公司主辦的「AI × RWA 投資論壇 2026」，將於 11 月 3 日在香港尖沙咀舉行。

本次論壇特別邀請兩位神秘重磅大咖，將於後續晚間酒會環節登場，帶來獨家行業內幕與前沿機會。

論壇將透過四場主題演講及一場圓桌對談，聚焦美股投資機會、企業上市、券商與交易所的發展，以及證券 RWA 的合規與商業機遇。四場主題演講後，嘉賓將共同探討 AI 如何創造可投資的資產價值。

1. 傳統金融 × RWA：探討傳統金融與資產代幣化的連接，以及金融機構的參與方式。
2. AI × 資產價值：討論 AI 如何改善資產的營運效率與價值，以及投資人如何評估相關機會。
3. 美股 × Web3 × 全球資本：從不同市場與投資視角出發，探討資產、機構及資本生態之間的合作。
